Just read the following Para carefully from Nephrocare's concall and understand why Dialysis is a difficult business to be profitable at.

Dialysis looks like a wonderful business on paper i.e. recurring revenue, non-discretionary demand, a patient who comes back three times a week for years. NephroPlus is the cleanest Indian case study for why it isn't, and the numbers are unusually honest about it.

1. You don't set the price. The payer does.

This is the root problem. Dialysis pricing in India runs around $22–25 per session, while the Philippines operates at roughly $110 per treatment for the identical clinical procedure, same machine, same consumables, 4–5x the realisation. That gap has nothing to do with cost or quality; it reflects what the payer can afford. In India the payer is largely the government (PPP tenders), insurance schemes, or a price-sensitive self-payer. You bid for volume in a tender; you don't price to value.

Watch how NephroPlus actually improved its realisation: blended RPT rose 13.3% in FY26 to ₹2,598, and 9.2% in Q1FY27 to ₹2,733. But that's mix, not pricing power as international went from 12% of revenue in FY23 to ~41% in 9MFY26 and 45% by Q1FY27. The company fixed its unit economics by leaving India, not by winning in it.

2. Cost per session is fixed, imported, and non-negotiable.

Dialyzer, tubing, dialysate, needles, EPO, plus nurse and technician time, every session consumes roughly the same basket. Machines and RO plants are largely imported. So you have a capped price and a floor on variable cost. Gross margin per session is structurally thin, and the only lever left is utilisation.

3. Utilisation is the whole game, but geography fights you.

Management says it plainly: dialysis is fundamentally a scale-driven business where higher volume drives operating leverage, asset utilisation and ROCE. But dialysis is a four-hour treatment required multiple times a week, which makes proximity critical as over 75% of NephroPlus's Indian clinics sit in tier-2 and tier-3 cities. Patients won't travel, so you must build small clinics close to them. Small clinics mean few machines, and a machine either runs its three shifts or it doesn't. Breakeven is a step function, not a curve. A greenfield clinic takes about 12 months to reach operational breakeven versus 3–4 months for an acquired one — so every year of expansion carries a drag cohort.

4. The financial history is the evidence.

Founded 2009–10. Raised roughly $205M across 13 rounds from 33 investors. For first 11 years of its life, Nephro was EBITDA negative and for 13 years it was PAT negative. High fixed cost businesses need massive scale to generate margins.

One of the easiest mistakes in investing is annualising a great quarter.

Valiant Laboratories just reported ~25% operating margins in Q1 FY27.

The stock quickly moved from roughly Rs. 60 to Rs. 95.

And there are genuine reasons for the improvement.

Valiant has backward integrated into Acetic Anhydride, one of the key raw materials used in manufacturing Paracetamol API.

Another important raw material, PAP, is largely imported into India from China. Valiant, however, sources it from its group Company, Valiant Organics.

So the improvement in economics is real.

But here is the problem.

Paracetamol API is not structurally a 25%+ margin business.

It is closer to a 10–15% margin business under normal economics.

Which means the mistake would be to take this quarter's profitability and assume this is the new base.

If margins normalise from 25% towards historical industry economics, earnings can look very different from what annualising Q1 suggests.

And Valiant is probably not the only example.

Q1 FY27 has thrown up some spectacular results across Companies. But a great quarter does not necessarily mean the earnings trajectory has permanently changed.

The real question is not how good the quarter was.

It is how much of that quarter is sustainable.

That distinction becomes especially important when the stock price has already started extrapolating the good news.

MODISONS

The tiny component sitting inside India’s electrification story

Most people have never heard of Modison. But its products sit inside the equipment that controls some of the most critical electricity infrastructure.

Modison manufactures electrical contacts and contact materials used in circuit breakers, contactors and switchgear across low, medium, high and extra-high voltage applications. Its portfolio includes silver-alloy contacts, copper-tungsten contacts, crowns, brazing assemblies, bimetal rivets, cladded contacts and specialised alloys. In simple words, Modison makes the tiny metal parts that connect and disconnect electricity safely.

And this is where the story gets interesting.

In high-voltage contacts, Modison estimates it has ~80–82% market share in India and says it is the only Indian manufacturer of specialised “crowns”. These components are designed into breakers supplied to customers such as GE, ABB, Siemens, BHEL and BEL. Replacing a qualified contact supplier is not like changing a normal vendor — the component has to be tested and qualified for the specific breaker design, creating years of switching friction.

The ISRO example shows how difficult this capability can be to replicate. ISRO had reportedly tried 5–6 suppliers over 5–6 years for a Russian-standard brazing alloy foil. Modison developed the import substitute in just 8–10 months and became the qualified domestic supplier. That is much more interesting than simply saying “Modison has good technology.”

There is another important advantage: Modison is vertically integrated. It can refine silver, manufacture contact materials and then manufacture the finished contacts itself. It also has an in-house tool room, R&D capability and testing infrastructure. Around 260 new customer-specific products were developed in FY26 — these are not simple catalogue products, but parts designed around customer specifications.

Now comes the growth opportunity.

India is entering a long power-infrastructure cycle. More renewable generation means more transmission infrastructure. More factories, metros, EV infrastructure and data centres mean more switchgear. Management specifically highlighted data centres and AI as a demand driver because more data-centre power infrastructure requires more switchgear and therefore more electrical contacts.

The pipeline is broader than just India. Modison wants exports to cross ₹100 crore in FY27 and has identified 20–25 large international prospects. It is also working on high-voltage products, silver-thrifting solutions, specialised alloys and tungsten recovery. The company has set revenue targets of ₹880 crore for FY27 and ₹1,365 crore by FY30.

But investors need to understand one very important catch.

Modison is not yet a pure high-margin specialty company.

Around 80% of sales come from low/medium-voltage products, where management estimates only ~30–35% Indian market share and where silver accounts for 75–80% of raw-material cost. FY26 revenue jumped 45% to ₹716 crore and EBITDA rose 143% to ₹115 crore, but a large part of the reported growth was helped by the huge increase in silver prices.

This is why I would not simply extrapolate FY26 margins.

The real test for Modison is whether it can gradually shift the mix from “silver conversion” to “mission-critical engineering.”

If high-voltage contacts, crowns, specialised alloys, exports, data-centre demand and grid infrastructure become a much larger part of the business, the quality of earnings could improve materially.

If not, Modison could remain a cyclical silver-processing business with a very attractive niche attached to it.

That is the real investment question.

The moat is real. The opportunity is real. But the next few years will tell us whether Modison can turn a small high-voltage toll bridge into the main highway.

reports.text:
Gaja Capital is raising funds through an IPO primarily to meet its own sponsor commitments in its AIF structures, including offshore vehicles.

A key question is — if the existing sponsor capital has already increased by nearly 20% in the last year, why does the company need to raise fresh capital from public investors to invest further in these high-risk, illiquid assets?

Interestingly, around 85% of Gaja’s income comes from management fees and carried interest, while income from sponsor commitments contributes only about 10%.

This raises a fundamental question: a significant portion of the fresh issue proceeds is being deployed toward an activity that currently contributes a relatively small share of revenue.

Moreover, carried interest is dependent on successful exits and realisation of investment gains. Until portfolio investments are monetised, the carried interest recorded in financial statements may not necessarily translate into actual cash inflows.

The key investor question is whether the additional sponsor commitments will create enough incremental value through future fee income and carry generation to justify the capital being raised

Company & Business
- 50+ years of industrial-gas operating history.
- Produces oxygen, nitrogen, argon and hydrogen.
- Also manufactures CO₂, acetylene and specialty gases.
- Serves steel, healthcare and pharmaceutical industries.
- Also supplies fabrication and shipbuilding customers.

Three Supply Models
- Bulk gas supplied to industrial customers.
- Packaged gases supplied through cylinders.
- On-site plants operate within customer facilities.
- On-site contracts can run 15+ years.
- Pipeline integration creates strong switching barriers.

Regional Moat
- Installed-capacity leader in West Bengal.
- Strong position across Andhra Pradesh.
- Also leads installed capacity in Telangana.
- Gas transportation becomes expensive over distances.
- Regional proximity creates meaningful competitive advantage.

On-Site Business
- On-site revenue reached ₹45.7 Cr in FY25.
- Revenue stood at ₹5.1 Cr in FY23.
- Business expanded nearly 9x in two years.
- Customer contracts provide long-term revenue visibility.
- Customer-linked plants reduce demand risk.

On-Site Economics
- Certain customers fund plant investment.
- Customers may also bear electricity costs.
- Ellenbarrie can access surplus gas.
- Surplus gas can serve merchant customers.
- Model can improve capital efficiency.

Industry Opportunity
- India's on-site penetration: 16.8%.
- Global on-site penetration: 28.2%.
- Significant penetration gap remains.
- Industrial customers can increasingly adopt on-site supply.
- Structural demand supports long-term growth.

Near-Term Capacity Expansion
- Uluberia-II plant has been commissioned.
- Jai Balaji plant: 320 TPD capacity.
- Jai Balaji plant expected from Q2 FY27.
- Plant backed by long-term contract.
- Capacity addition linked to identified demand.

Large Merchant Expansion
- FY27–FY28 capex planned: ~₹450 Cr.
- Two merchant plants planned.
- Target regions: North and West-Central India.
- Combined capacity: ~450–500 TPD.
- Expansion significantly increases addressable market.

Merchant Expansion Risk
- New capacity currently lacks advance contracts.
- New regions have established competitors.
- Linde remains a major competitor.
- Inox Air Products also has presence.
- Air Liquide adds competitive pressure.
- Utilisation ramp-up remains critical.

Argon Opportunity
- Argon produced as oxygen by-product.
- Demand linked to speciality steel.
- Fabrication demand supports consumption.
- Solar manufacturing adds another demand driver.
- Tight supply can support better realisations.

Margin Quality
- Rising EBITDA margin needs careful interpretation.
- On-site mix materially improves reported margins.
- Customers may directly bear electricity costs.
- Revenue per tonne has declined significantly.
- Higher margins do not solely reflect pricing power.

Cash Flow & Returns
- Company has history of negative free cash flow.
- Large capex increases execution requirements.
- New plants must achieve strong utilisation.
- Cash conversion remains an important monitorable.
- Returns on new capacity need validation.

KEY MONITORABLES
- New customer contracts for merchant plants.
- Plant utilisation as capacity ramps.
- Free cash flow generation.
- Argon pricing and availability.
- Sustainability of ~40% EBITDA margin.
- Returns from FY27–FY28 capex.

KEY TAKEAWAY
- Genuine regional industrial-gas business.
- On-site model provides structural customer stickiness.
- India's low penetration offers growth runway.
- Capacity expansion creates significant opportunity.
- Merchant expansion also brings execution risk.
- Next two years will test scalability.

JP MORGAN ON GOLD LENDERS

IIFL, preferred pick, is in early stages of a turnaround & should re-rate on higher profitability; while Muthoot’s YTD underperformance offers a compelling entry point

Manappuram's turnaround has just begun, with 1Q27 print a confirmation

Gold loans in India are secured retail credit with robust growth (65% 2Y CAGR), & next phase of growth should be structural rather than cyclical

Gold loans’ share of system credit could reach 10% over next 5Y from 2%/5% as of FY24/26
Driver is a multi-year cultural shift, as gold evolves from a family heirloom to a monetizable asset

This is moving borrower preference from unsecured & small business loans towards gold, facilitated by rising financial literacy of borrowers & reduced risk appetite of lenders

Borrowers benefit from a 300-600bps rate arbitrage, while lenders grow a low-risk secured book

Gold loan penetration remains low despite recent surge, with only 11% of bottom-60% household gold collateralised

Competition is intensifying, but high barriers to entry (TAT, distribution, branch network) should protect incumbents’ profitability.

JPM commodities team forecasts gold at $5k/oz by end-2027 (11% upside) which bodes well for gold-NBFCs, given high correlation of 90-95% between gold and stock prices (ex-IIFL)

Bernstein on SBI Cards
U-P, TP cut to Rs 430 from Rs 610

Revolver-led credit card model is undergoing a structural disruption, with little evidence that pressure is easing, let alone reversing.

SBI Cards, as a pure-play credit card issuer, has borne brunt of this shift

Continue to see downside risk from further declines in revolvers-to-spends ratio, which should keep NIMs & earnings growth under pressure despite improving credit costs

Accordingly, revise EPS estimates lower, leaving us 19% & 28% below consensus in FY28E & FY29E

For SBI Cards, decline in revolvers-to-spends ratio (from 7% in 2019 to 2.8% in 1Q27) has translated into a sharp reduction in profit generated per unit of spends

Importantly, fall in revolvers has not been offset by growth in EMI loans, as EMI balances-to-spends ratio has also declined

While company has limited the earnings impact through lower operating expenses, this has now started to impact the fees/non-interest income-to-spends ratio.

✅ Company says there has been no disruption to Lenskart, the group company or its customers.

🇸🇬 The Singapore group company has notified the concerned data privacy regulator in compliance with applicable law.

🟡 Impact: Neutral — incident has been contained with no reported disruption to operations or customers.

MILLWORKS TECHNOLOGIES: SECURES ₹53.74 CR ORDERS; ORDER BOOK RISES TO ₹121.88 CR

📦 Company secured multiple domestic and international purchase orders worth ₹53.74 Cr during July 21–August 19, 2026.

✈️ Orders are primarily from aerospace, defence, railway and semiconductor sectors, covering precision-machined components and integrated assemblies.

📈 With these wins, FY27 confirmed order book has increased to ₹121.88 Cr, providing stronger revenue visibility.

🛡️ Investee company Quick Pay has delivered AASHVAST Lab for the Indian Army, an offline evaluation facility for military electronics.

🚀 Management expects the expanded order book and defence capabilities to support sustained business growth and operational momentum in the near-to-medium term.

🟢 Impact: Positive — strong order inflows, rising order-book visibility and increasing exposure to aerospace & defence strengthen the growth outlook.

SPR AUTO TECHNOLOGIES: RAISES ₹1,000 CR THROUGH QIP

📊 Company allotted 23,36,448 equity shares at ₹4,280/share to 45 institutional investors.

💵 Total QIP size stands at approximately ₹1,000 Cr.

🏷️ Issue price represents a 3.56% discount to the floor price of ₹4,438.20/share.

🏦 Key allottees include Prazim Trading & Investment (11%), Abu Dhabi Investment Authority–Monsoon (7%), ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund–Active Momentum (7%), SBI Automotive Opportunities Fund (7%) and Kotak Small Cap Fund (6.09%).

📈 Other investors include Axis MF, Motilal Oswal MF, Aditya Birla Sun Life MF, UTI MF, HSBC MF, BlackRock and Edelweiss funds.

🟢 Impact: Positive — ₹1,000 Cr institutional fundraise significantly strengthens the company's capital base, though the equity issuance results in shareholder dilution.

METROPOLIS HEALTHCARE: SUBSIDIARY TO RAISE ₹10 CR VIA CONVERTIBLE PREFERENCE SHARES

💰 Metropolis Quality Solutions Private Limited (MQSPL) approved issuance of 10,00,000 Optionally Convertible Redeemable Preference Shares (OCRPS) at ₹10 each, aggregating to ₹10 Cr.

👤 The OCRPS will be allotted to Dr. Puneet Kumar Nigam, former Chief Quality Officer of Metropolis Healthcare and promoter/promoter group of MQSPL.

📊 Upon successful subscription and subsequent conversion of OCRPS into equity shares, MQSPL will cease to be a wholly-owned subsidiary of Metropolis Healthcare.

🏢 However, MQSPL will continue to remain a subsidiary of Metropolis Healthcare.

📌 MQSPL is yet to commence business operations and has not contributed to Metropolis' revenue, income or net worth.

🟡 Impact: Neutral — transaction brings external capital into MQSPL while Metropolis retains subsidiary control, but its ownership stake will be diluted upon conversion.

WELSPUN CORP: SECURES LARGEST-EVER SINGLE ORDER WORTH ~₹17,200 CR

💰 Welspun Corp secured its largest single order in company history, valued at approximately $1.8 billion (~₹17,200 Cr).

🇺🇸 Order is for supply of pipes manufactured at the company's USA facility.

📅 The order will be executed between FY28 and FY29.

📈 With this order, Welspun Corp's global order book reaches a record $4.4 billion (~₹42,100 Cr).

🏗️ The deal significantly strengthens multi-year revenue visibility and the company's position in the North American energy infrastructure market.

🟢 Impact: Strongly Positive — record order substantially boosts the order book and provides strong long-term revenue visibility.

NETWEB TECHNOLOGIES: QIP CLOSED; RAISES ~₹1,200 CR

📊 Company approved allotment of 25,05,219 equity shares to qualified institutional buyers.

💵 QIP issue price fixed at ₹4,790/share.

📉 Issue price represents a 1.96% discount to the floor price of ₹4,885.90/share.

🏦 Total QIP size works out to approximately ₹1,200 Cr.

✅ QIP opened on August 17 and closed on August 20, 2026.

🟢 Impact: Positive — sizeable capital raise strengthens the company's balance sheet and provides funds to support future growth.

PN GADGIL JEWELLERS: TO ACQUIRE 100% STAKE IN SILVOSTYLE JEWELLERS FOR ₹27.96 CR

🏢 Company approved acquisition of 100% equity stake in Silvostyle Jewellers Ltd (SJL) for ₹27.96 Cr.

💰 Acquisition will be undertaken at ₹18.64/share through subscription to fresh shares and purchase of shares from existing shareholders.

📊 Of the total consideration, ₹27.68 Cr will be infused as fresh capital into SJL for its business purposes, while ₹0.28 Cr will be paid to existing shareholders.

🤝 SJL is part of the PN Gadgil Jewellers promoter group, and the transaction will be undertaken at arm’s length.

💍 Acquisition aims to strengthen and consolidate PN Gadgil’s jewellery business, create operational synergies, broaden product offerings and strengthen market presence.

🏬 Upon completion, Silvostyle Jewellers will become a wholly-owned subsidiary of PN Gadgil Jewellers.

🟢 Impact: Positive — acquisition strengthens the jewellery business and provides fresh growth capital to SJL while expanding PN Gadgil’s operating platform.

HINDUSTAN COMPOSITES: COMPLETES SLUMP SALE OF FRICTION BUSINESS TO RANE (MADRAS)

🤝 Company completed the slump sale of its Friction Business Undertaking to Rane (Madras) Ltd, effective August 20, 2026.

👔 Four senior management personnel from Sales, Purchase, Works and R&D will be transferred to Rane (Madras) as part of the transaction.

📌 Managing Director Pawan Kumar Choudhary will also transfer to Rane (Madras) and has consequently resigned as MD & KMP of Hindustan Composites.

🏢 Choudhary will, however, continue as a Non-Executive Director of Hindustan Composites.

🟢 Impact: Positive/Neutral — completion of the friction business divestment executes the company's restructuring plan, though the transaction also results in transfer of key senior management to Rane (Madras).

Advit Jewels Limited – Q1 FY27 Earnings Conference Call Highlights

Company Overview:
Advit Jewels Limited is a Jaipur-based luxury jewellery company specializing in Kundan, Polki, Diamond, and Studded Jewellery. Backed by a family legacy dating back to 1921, the Company follows an integrated business model encompassing in-house design, manufacturing, stone setting, polishing, and quality control, serving customers across India through its design-led and quality-focused approach.

Financial Performance:

Q1 FY27 Highlights
* Total Income of ₹3,540.24 Lakhs, YoY growth of 37.35% 
* EBITDA of ₹1,172.45 Lakhs, YoY growth of 33.02% 
* EBITDA Margin of 33.12% 
* Net Profit of ₹818.68 Lakhs, YoY growth of 37.86% 
* Net Profit Margin of 23.12%, YoY growth of 9 Bps 
* EPS of ₹2.46, YoY growth of 32.26%

Business & Operational Highlights:

Market Presence & Channel Strategy
* B2B contributed approximately 78% of Q1 revenue, while B2C contributed 22%, with bridal jewellery remaining the key demand driver across both channels.
* The Company plans to significantly scale B2C while continuing to strengthen its B2B business, with a focus on building a differentiated luxury boutique experience.
* Demand for branded designer jewellery is increasingly expanding beyond HNI customers, particularly among younger consumers.

Product Strategy & Innovation
* Continued focus on handcrafted Kundan, Polki and Jadau jewellery, while expanding into contemporary men's jewellery and lightweight prêt jewellery.
* The Company is using lighter gold weights with greater use of stones and Polki to maintain product appeal and affordability amid higher gold prices.

Jaipur Flagship Store
* A 30,000 sq. ft. flagship store is being developed in Jaipur, targeted for launch in November, although execution may face some delays due to heavy rains in the city.
* The flagship is intended to act as a hub for the wider retail network, supporting inventory rotation and customer conversion across locations.

Franchise Expansion
* The Company is developing a franchise model for Tier 2 and smaller cities, while company-owned stores will be prioritized in major metropolitan markets.
* Franchise protocols are expected to be finalized within approximately one month, with a typical franchise store requiring ₹6–8 Cr of jewellery inventory funded by the franchise partner.

Market Expansion:
* The Company continues to strengthen its national presence while exploring international opportunities across the US, UK and Middle East.
* International expansion is expected to be driven through exhibitions, shows and private events, with initial focus on building brand awareness.
* The long-term objective is to establish Rambhajo as a globally recognized Indian luxury handcrafted jewellery brand.

Management Commentary & Outlook
* Management remains confident of sustaining growth momentum.
* B2C expansion, the Jaipur flagship, franchise rollout and product innovation are expected to be key growth drivers going forward.
* The Company remains focused on building Rambhajo as a differentiated luxury jewellery brand in India, followed by a gradual international expansion.

Very interesting fact in SEBI study on Retail participation in F&O released: 

“More the capital, lower the losses.”

77% of traders had a peak margin less than ₹1Lac, 16% has a peak margin between ₹1Lac and 5Lac, Only 0.4% had a margin more than ₹1Cr.

When it came to losses, while 90% of the 77% customers having a margin below ₹1Lac make losses, amongst those 0.4% having more than ₹1Cr loss makers were only 36%.

So, More the Capital, lower the losses. 

Simply put, if you don’t have bigger capital, better avoid trading in options.

One of the most striking observation in SEBI study on Retail F&O participation for FY26, released: 

Amongst all F&O traders, in FY26, 93% of all F&O Traders were pure Option Buyers. 90% of these option buyers made losses.

Inversely, only 2.1% of all F&O traders were majorly option sellers. 56% were profitable.

*Conclusion: Better to be an option seller, then being an option buyer*

Gaja Capital is raising funds through an IPO primarily to meet its own sponsor commitments in its AIF structures, including offshore vehicles.

A key question is — if the existing sponsor capital has already increased by nearly 20% in the last year, why does the company need to raise fresh capital from public investors to invest further in these high-risk, illiquid assets?

Interestingly, around 85% of Gaja’s income comes from management fees and carried interest, while income from sponsor commitments contributes only about 10%.

This raises a fundamental question: a significant portion of the fresh issue proceeds is being deployed toward an activity that currently contributes a relatively small share of revenue.

Moreover, carried interest is dependent on successful exits and realisation of investment gains. Until portfolio investments are monetised, the carried interest recorded in financial statements may not necessarily translate into actual cash inflows.

The key investor question is whether the additional sponsor commitments will create enough incremental value through future fee income and carry generation to justify the capital being raised

Retail Losses

- FY25 active traders stood at 1.06 Cr.
- First participation decline since FY16.
- ~45.7 lakh traders exited trading.
- Trader exits accelerated 76%.
- New entrants fell 40% to 20.8 lakh.

Options Dominate Retail Trading
- 99.3% of individuals traded options.
- 93% traded only options.
- 97% were predominantly options buyers.
- ~90% of options buyers incurred losses.
- Average options-buyer loss: ~₹1.28 lakh.
- Median RoCE for buyers: -114%.

Options Buyers vs Sellers
- Options sellers had 43.8% loss incidence.
- Average seller loss: ₹51.7 lakh.
- Seller losses were over 11x buyer losses.
- Buyers lose more frequently.
- Sellers face much larger losses when losing.

Trading Behaviour
- 85% of trading quarters were loss-making.
- Median loss exceeded twice median gain.
- Only 0.5% stayed profitable every year.
- 92% of consecutive-year losers kept losing.
- 24% had no cash-market turnover.

Capital & Concentration
- 77% used below ₹1 lakh capital.
- These traders generated only 8% turnover.
- 42% traders generated 94% turnover.
- High-intensity traders dominate market activity.
- 77% of past losers had small portfolios.

Young Trader Participation
- 43% of derivatives traders were below 30.
- 89% of under-30 traders lost money.
- New young entrants declined sharply.
- Retail derivatives participation is cooling.

Trading Costs
- Individual traders incurred ~₹25,000 Cr costs.
- STT paid reached ₹6,645 Cr.
- STT increased 35% YoY.
- Transaction costs materially impact retail returns.

KEY TAKEAWAY
- Retail F&O participation declined sharply.
- Options remain the dominant retail segment.
- Options buyers lose more frequently.
- Options sellers face larger loss severity.
- High-frequency traders drive most turnover.
- Persistent profitability remains extremely rare.

Why is Morepen Labs getting rerated so sharply?
The story has changed on 3 fronts:

1. CDMO finally starts contributing. 
The ₹849 Cr CDMO order is now showing up in numbers. Q1 itself saw ~₹58 Cr of CDMO commercial supplies, with a much larger contribution expected ahead.

2. Operating leverage is kicking in. 
Q1 revenue jumped to ₹570 Cr, while EBITDA margin expanded to ~15% and PAT jumped to ₹56 Cr vs ₹11 Cr YoY.

3. The market is now seeing earnings visibility. 
Morepen was earlier largely valued as a steady API/medical-device business. The CDMO opportunity changes the potential growth and margin profile.

My FY27 assumptions:
Revenue: ₹2,400–2,500 Cr
EBITDA margin: 14–15%
PAT margin: 9–10%
PAT: ₹216–250 Cr

At a ₹5,281 Cr market cap, this implies roughly 21–24x FY27 P/E.
If CDMO execution continues, margins hold, and repeat orders start coming in, the rerating story could have further legs. 
These are strictly my assumptions, NOT management guidance. 
The biggest question now: Is this the beginning of a sustainable CDMO business or just a one-order earnings spike?

EV scooters crossed 10% of all 2-wheeler sales in India for first time in June 2026. Ather delivered 2.39 lakh units in FY26, growing 83%. Hero VIDA delivered 1.44 lakh, growing 196%. 

At that volume, software revenue adds up fast. If 94% of 2.39 lakh Ather buyers pay Rs 14,000 to Rs 20,000 for tech packs, that is roughly Rs 170 Cr just from software per year.

SUGAR STOCKS ; GOVT IMPOSES SUGAR STOCK LIMIT ON BULK CONSUMERS ⚠️

📢 New Order: Government introduces the Sugar (Stockholding Limit of Bulk Consumers) Order, 2026, effective September 1 to November 30, 2026.

🏭 Stock Limit: Bulk consumers using more than 10 metric tonnes of sugar per month cannot hold sugar inventory exceeding 15 days of consumption.

🥤 Who It Covers: Confectioners, soft-drink manufacturers, food-processing companies, sweetmeat sellers and other institutional buyers consuming at least 10 MT per month on average.

📊 Monitoring: Sugar purchases and consumption will be verified using GST returns and applicable sugar HSN codes.

📦 Market Impact: The restriction could discourage large-scale inventory accumulation and increase availability of sugar in the market.

First CAS Manipulation found.

SEBI has passed an ex-parte interim order against an FPI and a local stockbroker, for what it calls prima facie manipulation of CAS on 13 August and wrongful gains of ₹3.67 crore.

What really happened?

It was Sensex weekly expiry. Inside the auction window the index moved 362 points in two seconds, then 405 points in 28 seconds.

1. Copthall Mauritius was 86.6% of the entire gross buy value in that auction. Every order across all 30 Sensex stocks at exactly 3% above reference price, the maximum the band allows. Then it cancelled ₹98 crore of them once the move had happened. 

It held long calls and short puts on that expiry. Spent ₹57 lakh in the cash market, made ₹2.96 crore in derivatives.

2. Mansi Share and Stock Broking did the reverse. 

₹145 crore of sell orders below reference price, holding the index down while it exited its long puts, then cancelled 99% of them in three seconds. 

That cancellation alone moved the Sensex 233 points.

A chemicals company with 45+ years of legacy in pyridine and acetic anhydride just paid ₹189.2 crore for 40% of an electronics design firm. Sounds like random diversification. It isn't.

Jubilant Ingrevia already sells into the semiconductor value chain, just one layer down. Its CDMO arm makes ultra-high-purity chemicals for chip and display manufacturing: E-Pyridine, E-Choline, photoresist precursors, display intermediates. The fab customer relationships already exist.

What Jubilant structurally cannot build in-house is what Zettaone brings. Co-founded about two decades ago, it does R&D, design, prototyping, manufacturing, assembly and box build for aerospace, defence, semiconductor, automotive, medical and industrial customers. The pitch to those shared customers becomes: we don't just supply your chemicals, we can design and build your electronics too.

Zettaone's turnover: ₹51.1cr in FY24, ₹79.1cr in FY25, ₹98.1cr in FY26. Growth decelerating from +55% to +24%.

₹189.2cr for 40% implies roughly ₹473cr for the whole company, about 4.8x sales.

40% makes Zettaone an associate, not a subsidiary. It won't consolidate. Jubilant gets an equity-accounted share of profit and no control over the business it's backing.

A genuinely interesting angle on India's electronics localisation push, entered through a side door nobody was watching.
